subject: Dedicated Capacity: run-rate, GPU classification, and SLA matrix
messages:
From: Aman Singh <aman.singh@cloudwave.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Iyer <priya.iyer@cloudwave.com>
Date: 2027-04-28T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarification: dedicated reservation run-rate and GPU mapping

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed with the latency and the clear breakdown of cost controls. Procurement and infra asked for a few clarifications to finalize the RFP response. Could you confirm the following so we can complete the sizing workbook on our side?

1) Run-rate vs peak: For our projected 12-month run-rate of 250M tokens/day with 2.5x daily peak, what mixed GPU footprint would you recommend to meet a 95th pct tail latency of <200ms for chat workloads (sequence length ~1024)?

2) GPU classes: You mentioned H100 and A100-80GB hot lanes and L40S for cost-optimized batches. Can you provide the expected tokens/sec (for the model family we discussed — transformer 70B) per GPU and an example packing strategy?

3) Reservation flexibility: We need sample commitment tiers (monthly reserved v. burst credits) and how burst credits degrade in saturation. Also provide minimum notice for increasing reserved pool and lead times.

4) Network / NVLink bandwidth: Any requirements for multi-node distributed serving when using model parallel sharding? We are concerned about intra-pod bandwidth for KV cache warmup with long chat histories.

If easier, send back a filled workbook and any SLA matrix you have. We plan to share this with our procurement committee on Friday.

Appreciate it — Aman
CloudWave Solutions

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Aman Singh <aman.singh@cloudwave.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laur en Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-28T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification: dedicated reservation run-rate and GPU mapping

Aman —

Thanks for the clear list. I've attached a populated workbook (CWS_RunRate_Workbook_v1.xlsx) and our Commitment & SLA matrix (RW-Commitment-SLA-Matrix.pdf). Short answers below; workbook has the run-rate math and three sizing scenarios (conservative / balanced / aggressive).

1) Run-rate vs peak: For 250M tokens/day (balanced scenario), we recommend a mixed pool: 35% H100 (hot lane), 50% A100-80GB (general-purpose), 15% L40S (spot/cost-optimized). That gives headroom for 2.5x peaks with autoscale + burst credits. We include a 10% safety buffer for KV cache cold starts.

2) GPU throughput examples (transformer 70B, seq 1024, batching tuned):
- H100 (8x HBM partition): ~4200–5200 tokens/sec per GPU for streaming infer with continuous batching
- A100-80GB: ~2600–3200 tokens/sec per GPU
- L40S (INT8/quantized path): ~1400–1800 tokens/sec per GPU (best for high-batch rerank/embeddings)

Packing suggestion: route low-latency conversational traffic to H100 hot lanes with smaller batch sizes (4–8), route background bulk generation and embeddings to A100/L40S with larger batches (32–128). Workbook includes expected QPS -> GPU mapping table.

3) Reservation flexibility: Typical tiers: 30%, 50%, 70% of projected run-rate reserved. Burst credits are issued as a monthly pool — they are consumed after reserved capacity is saturated and degrade by priority policies (hot-lane burst > general > cost-optimized). Lead times: resizing reserved pool upward requires 14 days for dedicated capacity rebalancing; downward changes are possible each invoice period with no penalty. Details in PDF.

4) Network: For multi-node model sharding we recommend at least 200 Gbps per node for stable KV warmup and <50ms cross-node latency for real-time chat. We provide network profiling (network-bandwidth-profile.csv) showing measured KV warmup times across different pod sizes.

Next steps: Ben will follow up with a brief technical addendum on kernel-fitment and packing heuristics, and Lauren will attach the proposed contract language for commitment tiers. If you want a short call to walk through the workbook before procurement review, propose two 30-min slots and we'll take one.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: CWS_RunRate_Workbook_v1.xlsx, RW-Commitment-SLA-Matrix.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Aman Singh <aman.singh@cloudwave.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-29T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification: dedicated reservation run-rate and GPU mapping (technical addendum)

Aman / Mina —

Adding the technical context Mina promised. A few specifics so your infra team can validate assumptions:

- Token/sec numbers above assume our optimized causal kernel path and continuous KV caching. Numbers will vary +/-10–15% with sequence length and prompt conditioning.

- A100 vs H100 differences: H100 benefits from FP8/structured sparsity optimizations for the 70B family, increasing tokens/sec by ~35% in our internal benchmarks when using fused attention kernels. A100-80GB remains more cost-stable for sustained throughput when KV fits comfortably in 80GB.

- Quantization: L40S path uses INT8 kernels; expect slightly higher variance on output quality for sensitive generation tasks. We recommend hybrid routing: deterministic outputs to H100/A100, high-volume non-sensitive jobs to L40S.

- Example packing: For a target 95th pct <200ms at 2.5x peak, a 100-GPU balanced pool (35 H100 / 50 A100 / 15 L40S) with aggressive short-window autoscale (scale step=10 GPUs, cooldown=30s) met the SLA in our synthetic replay tests. Workbook includes the replay trace.

- Multi-node network: If you plan >8-node pods with model sharding, ensure RDMA-capable interconnect and configure our KV pre-warm hooks to reduce early-step tail by ~30%.

Happy to jump on a quick call with your infra folks for micro-benchmarks.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Aman Singh <aman.singh@cloudwave.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-01T11:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification: dedicated reservation run-rate and GPU mapping (procurement terms)

Aman —

Following up with procurement-level details and the proposed commitment language. Highlights:

- Commitment tiers: Monthly reserved tokens equivalent to 30% / 50% / 70% of projected run-rate. Each tier includes a baseline discount (5% / 12% / 20%) off list committed compute price.

- Burst credits: Monthly pool equal to 20% of reserved tokens for 30% tier, 30% for 50% tier, 40% for 70% tier. Burst credits are drawn down FIFO and have day-level decay only if exceeding sustained usage for 3 consecutive billing cycles.

- SLA: 99.5% availability for reserved pool with latency SLO credits for missed tail (credit calculation in RW-Commitment-SLA-Matrix.pdf).

- Changes & lead times: Upsizing reserved capacity requires 14 calendar days notice; downsizing permitted at next billing cycle. Early termination: standard 60-day notice with pro-rated rebate on committed fees (see section 6 in PDF).

- Security/compliance: SOC 2 Type II & ISO 27001 evidence available; we can route Private (VPC) deployments if your legal requires customer-managed keys.

I attached the formal PDF with the SLA matrix and contract snippets. If the procurement committee needs redlines, we'll accept edits via DocuSign (link below) and can fast-track through legal within 48 hours for the 70% tier.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.net/prepare/123abc

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Business Operations — Redwood Inference

Attachment: RW-Commitment-SLA-Matrix.pdf

From: Aman Singh <aman.singh@cloudwave.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification: dedicated reservation run-rate and GPU mapping

Thanks Mina, Ben, and Lauren — this is very helpful. A few quick notes after a procurement + infra sync: 

- We prefer the 50% reserved tier with a 30% burst credit pool as a starting point. Please confirm a provisional layout with exact GPU counts for the balanced scenario and an expected monthly committed spend (ballpark).

- Infra asked for a short proof-run: can Redwood provide a 4-hour replay using our anonymized production trace on your staging fleet to validate the 95th pct latency? We'd like to schedule next week if possible.

- Legal will review the DocuSign; Aman/Procurement will share redlines by Tuesday.

If you can send the provisional balanced layout (GPU counts + monthly committed spend estimate) by EOD Monday, we'll include it in the packet for Friday's procurement review.

Best,
Aman Singh
Senior Cloud Architect — CloudWave Solutions
